headline: YouTube Shorts removes dislike button globally
summary: The update also brings double speed playback and a 'Clear mode'
details: YouTube Shorts has removed the dislike button completely, instead relying on 'Not Interested' and 'Don't recommend this channel' to tune user feeds. The change aims to provide a 'more meaningful way' to interact with content.

The platform has also introduced a 'Clear mode', similar to TikTok's clear mode, allowing users to turn off the interface for a cleaner viewing experience. Additionally, users can now play Shorts at double speed by tapping and holding on the screen.
The new settings are rolling out in most regions, although the rollout may be staggered. YouTube Shorts has become a significant player with 200 billion daily views as of last year.

The removal of the dislike button has received mixed reactions, with some users expressing concerns about being able to express contempt for low-quality content. However, others argue that the 'Not interested' and 'Don't recommend' options are a better way to avoid undesirable content.

headline: Payload v4 exposes collections to LLMs by default
summary: The MCP plugin for Payload CMS now exposes collections to LLMs by default. Users must opt-out to disable.
details: The Payload CMS plugin MCP has been updated to version 4, which exposes collections to Large Language Models (LLMs) by default. This change was made after a refactor, and users must now opt-out to disable individual tools.

The plugin allows users to define custom tools with the defineTool builder, taking input via zod v4. Collections that were never listed are now suddenly reachable through MCP, and users should review them to disable anything sensitive.
Templates are available to quickly answer FAQs or store snippets for re-use. Users are advised to review their collections and disable any sensitive tools to avoid accidental exposure.
